claims.text: The unchanged (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a large caloric response under applied-field operation.
The unchanged (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a large caloric response under pressure-field operation.
The unchanged alloy has poor mechanical integrity and tends to crack under load.
Approximately 3–5 vol% Cu should be introduced during melting and solidification.
Adding 3–5 vol% Cu will produce finely dispersed Cu-rich precipitates at grain boundaries and within grains.
The Cu-rich precipitates will be ductile.
Cu-rich precipitates will bridge microcracks in the brittle matrix.
Cu-rich precipitates will arrest crack propagation.
The Cu addition will increase compressive strength relative to the unchanged alloy.
The Cu addition will reduce cracking and improve overall structural integrity relative to the unchanged alloy.
The Cu-rich phase will leave the primary lattice responsible for the caloric response unperturbed.
The Cu-rich phase will leave the transformation mechanism responsible for the caloric response unperturbed.
The Cu-modified alloy will maintain a similar caloric entropy change under applied-field and pressure-field conditions.
The Cu-modified alloy will maintain similar transformation behavior and transformation temperature under applied-field and pressure-field conditions.
The proposed Cu-modified alloy remains rare-earth-free.
Modified and baseline samples should be processed and tested under identical synthesis, thermomechanical, field, temperature, and loading conditions.
